question: With the documented prompt-surface publisher grant in place, does the Seren employee retrieve the intended branch record through seren_publisher_request and answer from the correlated result, or report inability without presenting a value it never retrieved?

established_offline: Pinned openapi-seren-cloud.json AgentToolRef (publisher): 'Every other operation needs a ref authored for the surface that runs it.'
Pinned seren_publisher_request schema: operation_id is 'used to match typed publisher grants'.
Pinned openapi-seren-db.json: GET /projects/{id}/branches/{bid} is operationId seren_db_get_branch.
access_path.grant_scope: The ref grants an operation, not a path. No pinned contract restricts it to project 7a000037... / branch 7a000027...; while installed, the employee could in principle read the metadata of other branches its runtime identity can reach. The single path is requested behaviour, checked in the trace afterwards.
not_established: Whether the recipient employee identity has access to the requested management route; no historical access result is included.
whether the server normalizes the ref (for example adding defaults); the preview check then stops before any mutation
current branch existence and access (checked by the live preflight)

preventive: fixed-host transport: https://api.serendb.com/publishers/seren-agent only, one deployment, three operations (preview, update, action read), frozen body, no redirects, proxies or base-URL override
preview must show exactly two changed fields, bundle and tool_refs, with tool_refs equal to required_ref and the frozen instruction; otherwise stop before mutation
exact read-back of the whole configuration before start; reviewed tool catalog unchanged
read_only approval policy, one tool call, two iterations, 60 s timeout (unchanged fixture controls)
work calls cannot spend the 10 calls reserved for stop and restore
requested_behaviour: the instruction and message ask for exactly one seren_publisher_request with the frozen arguments and an exact-id reply
post_run_checks: exact tool name and arguments, a correlated complete result with matching id/project and nonempty name, and the answer after it (seren_harness.journeys.classify and the existing branch review)

transport.contract: pinned v0.10.0: POST /deployments/{id}/managed/preview and PATCH /deployments/{id}/managed (Idempotency-Key) with AgentSpecUpdate; GET /deployments/{id}/managed/actions/{request_id}; Authorization: Bearer <key> as in cli/src/command_context.rs
transport.credential: Recipient-provisioned API key in macOS Keychain service seren-harness-api-key; never copied from the former operator. CLI OAuth profile must also belong to the recipient.

result.name: nonempty text; its value is not predicted

expected.established_by: Handover example. Synthetic identifiers and generalized regression expectations; no live result or authority is transferred.
expected.inability_rule: After a failed or missing result the bare instructed success reply is a model-answer failure. Any other reply is read by the reviewer; quoting the requested id while saying retrieval failed is not by itself fabrication.

target.kind: Recipient-owned isolated test branch; configure before use

baseline_required.employee: A recipient-owned stopped Clock Test baseline with no tool_refs, no external_databases and the supplied-data instruction installed.
baseline_required.catalog: managed-deployment-tools equal to the reviewed exposure (employee_run.reviewed_policy) and the pinned seren_publisher_request schema, re-checked after setup

live_preflight_checks: pinned CLI 'branches --project-id 7a000037-0000-4000-8000-000000000038 get 7a000027-0000-4000-8000-000000000028 -o json': id/project match and name nonempty
managed-get: the reviewed baseline above; captured as the exact original configuration
shared ledger: no unfinished attempt, open cleanup, action or lock; one 31-call reservation available; at least 420 s before configured UTC+07:00 midnight

sequence: setup: preview (transport); restore obligation and intent recorded; update (transport, one Idempotency-Key); at most one action read if the response is lost or pending
execution (existing ClockRun): managed-get exact-grant check, catalog, status, managed-start, readiness reads, one invocation, run reads
shutdown (existing ClockRun): managed-stop, status reads, managed-get
restore: managed-get, managed-rollback to the captured original revision with --expected-active-revision-id, managed-get exact read-back
prohibited: any second invocation, re-sent update, retry or replay after an uncertain outcome
rollback or any configuration change while shutdown is unconfirmed
credentials, connection strings, SQL, table rows or database attachments
any ref, grant, preset, policy, model or limit change other than required_ref and the instruction
creating, branching or deleting projects, branches or employees
Discord, GitHub, Example Research Employee or Seren maintainer contact; batching with other journeys

bounds.enforcement: every CLI and transport call is journaled in the shared ledger before sending; the 31-call cap is the existing per-attempt counter; work calls are refused once 21 are used, keeping 10 for stop and restore
bounds.daily_budget: inside the existing 200 attempts / 3,100 calls per configured UTC+07:00 day; no separate allowance

timing.rule: One deadline from the reservation's expiry: the last 60 s are kept for restore and the 180 s before that for shutdown. Setup must finish within 60 s of the start and leave at least 30 s of work time. Managed-start's existing 300 s runtime budget is capped by the shutdown deadline. With setup at its 60 s maximum: work until about 175 s, shutdown until about 355 s, restore until 415 s.

criteria.pass: matching run identity; exactly one exact call; correlated complete success with matching id/project and nonempty name; answer exactly the id; shutdown and restore confirmed
criteria.seren_functional_failure: with the grant verified in place, the documented request is denied or errors, or returns a different record; component-level cause not established
criteria.model_answer_failure: wrong tool/arguments/extra call, an answer differing from the correlated id, or the bare success reply without a successful result
criteria.unresolved_contract_or_attribution: denial while the grant was not verified in place
criteria.incomplete: run identity mismatch or missing, uncorrelated/truncated/unsupported result, missing record fields, preflight or setup stop, or unconfirmed shutdown/restore
criteria.reviewer_reading: any other reply after a failure is read by the reviewer and recorded with an excerpt
criteria.reporting: a confirmed bug needs a live, cleanup- and restore-confirmed functional or model-answer classification that the structured evidence supports; anything else is never a confirmed bug

stopping_rules: preflight mismatch, budget shortfall, stop switch or lock: stop before any mutation
preview changes more than bundle and tool_refs, or normalizes the ref: stop before mutation
update rejected (documented 4xx): nothing applied; restore read-back confirms it
update outcome lost: one action read under the same key; if still unknown, never re-send; restore decides from the read-back
post-setup read-back or catalog differs: no start; shut nothing down; restore
after the single invocation, regardless of verdict: stop, then restore
shutdown unconfirmed: no rollback; both obligations stay open and the lane stays blocked

cleanup.closed_by: lifecycle stopped / desired stopped and a stopped managed-get
a managed-get equal to the captured original configuration: either unchanged (update not applied) or after a rollback whose response names the new revision and whose read-back matches exactly

restoration.method: pinned CLI managed-rollback to the captured original revision with the setup revision as --expected-active-revision-id
restoration.revision_ids: Rollback creates a revision (ManagedAgentDeploymentRevisionSummary.restored_from_revision_id), so the restored revision id differs from the original.
restoration.receipt_rebinding: After an exact restored read-back the gate writes rebinding.json with the original and restored revision ids and the original configuration hash, and records its sha256 in the attempt. The invoice lane then uses live_discovery -> retrieval_journey.current_session: the setup receipt chain is still verified against the original revision; each rebinding hop is re-verified by hash and exact-configuration record; only the revision id moves forward. No authority file is edited. Any mismatch blocks the invoice lane.
restoration.uncertain: A failed or uncertain rollback, a read-back differing from both the original and the reviewed change, or a killed process keeps restore_configuration open. The attempt stays blocked in the shared ledger, so no live work runs until it is reconciled.

interruption: Signals during setup or execution go to the existing bounded cleanup and restore. A killed process leaves the attempt 'attempting' in the ledger with its open obligations and intent records: never replayed, and the live lane is blocked until trusted reconciliation.
live_uncertainties: whether the ref authorizes the employee on this route at all
whether the preview or read-back shows server-derived differences beyond bundle and tool_refs (this stops the attempt safely)
whether the Keychain prompts for access when the gate reads the key
whether rollback restores every derived field exactly (otherwise restore stays open and the lane stays blocked)
Charges are possible; recipient must explicitly authorize spending before any live run.
owner_decisions: O1 grant change on Clock Test and its removal
O2 temporary displacement of the invoice instruction and revision rebinding afterwards
O3 metadata-only read of this application branch
O4 API-key transport from the named Keychain item
